Subject: Columbus Health Summit — closed-loop reconciliation and ROI request

Hi team,

Thanks again to everyone who supported the Columbus Health Summit sponsorship last week. Ava — thank you for hosting and sharing the on-site logistics.

We have a discrepancy between the pipeline credited to the event in HubSpot and the list CHN provided. Marketing ops flagged ~34 leads that landed as MQLs after the event, but sales sees only 18 associated opportunities tagged to the Columbus sponsorship. Before we escalate to Finance for the Q4 spend write-off, I need us to close the loop on attribution.

Ask: can Ops or Sales own a quick reconciliation? Specifically we need:
- The raw attendance capture (badge scans, sign-in list) mapped to HubSpot contact IDs
- Any inbound leads from campaign landing pages during Dec 1–10 window
- The export of opportunities created/closed in the same window with source/UTM fields

I've attached the sponsor package and an attendance template to make mapping easier. If we cannot agree on closed-loop mapping by EOD Dec 17, I will escalate for a credits/dispute decision.

Thanks — Soojin

Soojin Lee
Sr. Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference

Folks —

I pulled the HubSpot export for the period Dec 1–12. Key observations: 1) 28 new contacts with source=event_columbus_2026, but only 16 were marked with original_source_detail matching the sponsor landing form; 2) 11 contacts were merged after creation which may have stripped the event attribution; 3) HUB contact IDs do not perfectly match the CHN exhibitor IDs (different vendor IDs).

I attached the hubspot-export-CHS-q4.csv with contact_id and lifecycle_stage columns. I'm seeing 5 contacts that converted to opportunities and one opportunity credited to a different event (Virtual Circle 11/29).

Questions:
- Did CHN provide the vendor IDs we should be matching (they sent exhibitor IDs, not HubSpot IDs)?
- If a contact was merged, do we prefer the final contact to inherit the event source or the original? Ops typically keeps the most recent source.

I can run a join script if someone drops the CHN exhibitor->hubspot mapping in the shared Drive.

—Ben
Account Executive, Field Sales
ben_carter@redwood.ai

On Fri, Dec 11, 2026 at 10:15 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks —
>
> I pulled the HubSpot export for the period Dec 1–12. Key observations: 1) 28 new contacts with source=event_columbus_2026, but only 16 were marked with original_source_detail matching the sponsor landing form; 2) 11 contacts were merged after creation which may have stripped the event attribution; 3) HUB contact IDs do not perfectly match the CHN exhibitor IDs (different vendor IDs).

Thanks for pulling this, Ben — good catch. Marketing Ops confirmed that merges default to the most recent source unless we force original_source to persist. That explains a number of the missing tags. I also see that the landing form used a different UTM parameter (utm_medium=partner) which Ops didn't map back to event_columbus_2026.

Proposal: mark all contacts with any CHS_Partner* UTM to a temporary event_tag=columbus-2026-recon so we can run opportunity attribution consistently for this reconciliation. I can push the tag and then export the opportunity list for review.

I'm attaching a quick reconciled-lead-list-CHS.csv showing the 18 contacts Ben mentioned that clearly map to closed opportunities. If we accept the temporary tag, we should be able to reach consensus.

Laura Bennett
Marketing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

1) LAURA to push event_tag=columbus-2026-recon (Ops) by EOD 12/15
2) BEN to run a dedupe-join script between CHN exhibitor IDs and HubSpot exported contact_id (Ben) — due 12/16
3) PRIYOM to produce a final opportunity export and ROI calc (closed pipeline value credited to event) — due 12/17

I can own the final calculation and sign off for Sales if needed. Let's do a 30-minute sync Thursday morning (12/17 10:00 EST) to review final numbers. Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=columbus-roi-review

Subject: Re: Columbus Health Summit — closed-loop reconciliation and ROI request (final)

Team — great work and thanks for turning this around quickly. Summary and decisions from today's sync: 

1) Laura pushed event_tag=columbus-2026-recon and Ben completed the CHN->HubSpot join. Priyom produced the ROI workbook.
2) Final agreed counts: 22 unique contacts attributable to the event, 7 opportunities created in Q4, aggregated closed pipeline value credited to event = $489,000. (See attached reconciled export.)
3) The delta vs CHN's original 34-lead claim is explained by duplicate records (8) and partner overlap where registrants selected both CHS_PartnerA and CHS_PartnerB (4). We will provide CHN the mapping and a short note explaining the merge behavior.

Action items:
- Priyom to drop the final export and methodology into the shared Drive and send to Finance (by EOD 12/18).
- Soojin to prepare a short customer-facing reconciliation email to AVA summarizing numbers and next steps (draft due 12/18).
- Marcus to confirm whether we apply a partial credit (pro rata) to the partner promos or keep full credit to Redwood for the 7 opportunities — decision by 12/20.

Ava — I'm CC'ing you so CHN sees the final numbers. We'll send a short reconciliation note tomorrow and include the mapping files.

Thanks,
Soojin

Soojin Lee
Sr. Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
